title: Following Distance: the Two-Second Rule
whatItIs: Leave enough space to stop safely if the vehicle in front brakes suddenly. Measure it in seconds, so it grows with your speed.
keyFacts: On faster roads and in tunnels, leave at least a two-second gap to the vehicle in front.
On wet roads, at least double the gap. On icy roads, leave much more.
Measure it: note when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point, such as a sign, and count two seconds.
Reach that point within two seconds? You are too close: drop back.
If someone overtakes and pulls into the gap in front, drop back to keep a two-second gap.

onTheTest.question: In good conditions, what is the minimum gap you should leave on a fast road?
onTheTest.why: On faster roads, leave at least two seconds in good conditions, and at least double that on wet roads.

traps: Two seconds is the minimum on dry roads, not a target.
Wet road? Make it at least four seconds.
Being tailgated? Don't speed up to get away from them: keep your gap ahead.
